newsitem.title: USA: Cook County mulls $1 bln bad debt write off-paper.
newsitem.headline: Cook County mulls $1 bln bad debt write off-paper.

text.p: Cook County officials are considering writing off $1 billion in bad debts accumulated at a public hospital in Chicago over a 17-year period, Chicago Tribune reported Monday.

Cook County has exhausted all efforts at collecting the money for services rendered from 1975 to 1992 and the patient debt should be stricken from the books, County Bureau of Health Services Chief Ruth Rothstein said in a letter to a commissioner obtained by the Tribune, the newspaper reported.
Patients have rung up another $270 million in debts for services rendered since then that have not yet been declared uncollectable, the newspaper said.

Cook County has no formal policy for writing off debts and the proposal would require approval from the board of commissioners, which is expected to consider adopting guidelines in a meeting this month, the newspaper said.

An outside auditor for the county told the newspaper that a write-off would have no financial impact on the county or its bond rating and board President John Stroger told the Tribune it would have no impact on the operations of county health facilities or the construction of a new hospital.

The director of the Center for Health Policy Research at the University of California at Los Angeles, E. Richard Brown, said that the $1 billion in unpaid bills was not extraordinary and the Los Angeles County health system has "considerably larger" uncollectable debts, the Tribune reported.
